posts.author: AphoticAmaranth
posts.body:
Why don't you want to take a break?
If the intent is to get your game done as soon as possible, it might actually be more efficient to rest and recover so that you can dev better, than to attempt working while exhausted, which can potentially lead to mistakes and end up wasting more time.

Decided to check your profile out after reading your message!
It's normal to be burnout after dedicating yourself wholeheartedly to something you are passionate about...
As for motivation... Since I'm not familiar with you and what made you want to create your game I can but offer some questions that might (hopefully) help.
Questions such as: Why did you decide to tell this story?
Why did you fall in love with Art? and what do you want to accomplish with it?
Have you seen the world? if yes what do you like the most if not where would you want to go?
What color was the sky today? how did it made you feel? if you wanted to tell it in your game how would you do it.
No game is perfect, they are all made by humans, so don't blame yourself for any tiny mistake you see during dev, keep going because...
The reason why, that's really up to you to decide, I'm really nothing but a stranger I could never attempt to give you a THE reason for why you do what you do, as cringe as that may sound.
Lastly on the topic of financial success no doubt you know it but I'll say it regardless,
Marketing really can make or break sales, I'd advice you to do some "high quality" YouTube shorts for at least a month (realistically you should do it 6 months to a year before game release)
other than that I'm not sure what else I could advice you...
It's late over here and I already yapped a bunch
Cya!

1. I wanted to cover something hard that everyone has or will end up dealing with in there life, second of all I wanted to represent what it might be like to not be the most important person in your own life ('Joe's Life' is ironically not about Joe but his best friend) third I am thriving to truly create a story that is... well, real.
2. It started when I was about 10 and became captivated by how Concernedape's stardew valley was originally made by one person, prior to that I would Allways imagine thousands of peaple in a big office building working for some big company. that was my only idea of how a game was made but the thought one person making a game I was thoroughly impressed by was... amazing. At that point I knew I was going to make a game. Flash forward to november of 2023 I asked my mom if she'd buy rpgmaker VXA for me (it was on sale for 10 dollars) it was the only game engine I could comprehend myself using at the time. again flash forward summer of 2024 I realized I needed to make a soundtrack for my game wich introduced me to music. Music slowly but surly since then has become extremely important to me. When late 2024 came around in November I self published my first instrumental album about my life at the time, music has become a true outlet to express myself and that was when I realized what art trully ment to me and how I was ment to make it. (Also I have a relationship with a record label nowadays wich is nice)
3. this one is simple, first of all I want it to be successful. Everyone has a different idea of success, for me it is for a notable amount of peaple to play it and not only for entertainment but has an experience worth sharing.
4. i have only seen the world in photos aside from America wich is a shame to say, as for were i'd want to go probably France or... Japan? Probably France.
4. Today was overcast, wich, of course, means the sky was gray. It made me feel grateful for the way it looked. As for telling it in my game, I would make the narrative show how the day was feeling just 'different'. How it would effected there regular behavior and how it was connected to there memories. The music would be slow and mildly emotional.
Thank you for asking me those questions. I'v been needing that. They made me reflect upon myself in a meaningful way. Also thanks for the Advice. (I'm also yapping lol)

posts.author: Holder
posts.body:
Silent actors, assemble your party from choices of a large number of job classes.
And go.
Receive an objective, proceed to a designated destination, and then continue on the main quest from there. The roleplay aspect comes into managing the team you've selected.
A short game could have replay ability from what classes you select, fancy a challenge then pick all support type jobs or go all out with tank like classes with skills that grind down bosses with abilities.
There's then little pressure to do the whole 'The heroes journey' route (A great book by the way) and gives you more focus on creating situations in each place the player visits and less of what drives the individual characters in your party.

Take a deep breath love. Sit a moment, enjoy a hot beverage, take sock of your work so far, collect your thoughts. See what still needs doing, and what has been done so far. These final stages are always scary. Not only is the journey ending, but your work will soon be subject to the gaze of the public... There is no trick to this, you just have have to learn to deal with it or even enjoy the thrill.
